def measure(args, corpus, work):
    root = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(args.corpora), corpus['clone'])
    src = corpora.ready(corpus, os.path.abspath(args.corpora), sparse=False)
    if not src:
        sys.exit(f"{corpus['name']}: not installed; run `scripts/corpora.py setup` first")
    list_file, tsconfig = program_inputs(corpus['name'], src, work)
    print(f"{corpus['name']}: RDT", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    rdt_out = os.path.join(work, f"{corpus['name']}.rdt.json")
    rdt, rdt_components = tool_run(['node', '--max-old-space-size=8192', os.path.join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'rdt.mjs'),
                                    list_file, tsconfig, rdt_out], rdt_out)
    print(f"{corpus['name']}: react-docgen", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    rdg_out = os.path.join(work, f"{corpus['name']}.rdg.json")
    rdg, rdg_components = tool_run(['node', os.path.join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'rdg.mjs'), list_file, rdg_out], rdg_out)
    print(f"{corpus['name']}: Caliper", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    found = {(relative(c['file'], root), norm_name(c['name'])): set(c['props']) for c in rdg_components}
    caliper_found = caliper_components(args.bin, src, root)
    items, counts = reference(rdt_components, caliper_found, root)
    entry = {
        'commit': corpus['commit'],
        'caliper': caliper_run(args.bin, src, args.runs),
        'rdt': rdt,
        'react_docgen': rdg,
        'reference': counts,
        'recall': {'caliper': recall(items, caliper_found, caliper_layer_members(args.bin, src, root)),
                   'react_docgen': recall(items, found)},
    }
    if args.oracle:
        try:
            entry['oracle'] = oracle(args.bin, corpus['name'], src, root, work)
        except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError, KeyError) as error:
            entry['oracle'] = {'error': str(error)}

def same_reference(record, previous):
    """Whether `record` and `previous` were measured against references built by the same rules."""
    return record.get('reference_version', 1) == previous.get('reference_version', 1)


def findings(record, previous):
    """What got worse since `previous`: Caliper's time and memory by more than 10%, its recall by more than 2 points,
    which is not compared across references built by different rules."""
    out = []
    for name, entry in record['corpora'].items():
        old = previous.get('corpora', {}).get(name)
        if not old:
            continue

            if entry['caliper'][key] > SLOWER * old['caliper'][key]:
                out.append(f"{name}: {label} {old['caliper'][key]} -> {entry['caliper'][key]}")

            if now < before - RECALL_DROP:

    lines = [f"Caliper {record['caliper']}, median of {record['runs']} runs; RDT and react-docgen one run each. Whole "

             '| Corpus | Caliper | JSON | RDT | react-docgen |', '| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: |']
    for name, e in record['corpora'].items():
        cell = lambda t: f"{t['ms'] / 1000:.2f} s, {t['rss_mib']:,} MiB"
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {cell(e['caliper'])} | {e['caliper']['json_mb']} MB | {cell(e['rdt'])} | "
                     f"{cell(e['react_docgen'])} |")
    lines += ['', '### Reference (RDT, cleaned)', '',
              '| Corpus | RDT entries with props | Not components | Repeats merged | Reference | Same file | Paired | Unpaired |',
              '| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |']
    for name, e in record['corpora'].items():
        r = e['reference']
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {r['rdt_with_props']} | {r['excluded_total']} | {r['merged']} | {r['reference']} | "
                     f"{r['exact']} | {sum(r['paired'].values())} | {r['unpaired']} |")
    lines += ['', '### Reference items Caliper reports nowhere, by cause', '', '| Corpus | Cause | Items |', '| --- | --- | --: |']
    for name, e in record['corpora'].items():
        for cause, count in sorted(e['reference'].get('unmatched', {}).get('by_cause', {}).items(), key=lambda c: -c[1]):
            lines.append(f'| {name} | {cause} | {count} |')
    lines += ['', '### Recall against the reference', '',
              '| Corpus | Tool | Components | Own props | Own, with layers | `@types/react` props | `@types/react`, with layers |',
              '| --- | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |']
    for name, e in record['corpora'].items():
        for tool in ('caliper', 'react_docgen'):
            r = e['recall'][tool]
            # A tool that writes no layers (react-docgen) has the same count with and without them.
            kinds = ('components', 'own', 'own_layers', 'react', 'react_layers')
            lines.append(f'| {name} | {tool} | ' + ' | '.join(f'{100 * rate(r.get(k, r[k.removesuffix("_layers")])):.1f}%'
                                                              for k in kinds) + ' |')
    oracle_rows = [(n, e['oracle']) for n, e in record['corpora'].items() if 'oracle' in e]
    if oracle_rows:
        lines += ['', "### TypeScript 7.1's checker (information)", '', '| Corpus | Shared props | Agree | Wrong |',
                  '| --- | --: | --: | --: |']
        for name, o in oracle_rows:
            lines.append(f'| {name} | unavailable: {o["error"][:80]} | | |' if 'error' in o else
                         f"| {name} | {o['shared_props']:,} | {100 * o['agree']:.1f}% | {100 * o['wrong']:.2f}% |")
    if reference_changed is not None:
        lines += ['', f"Recall was not compared with last week's: its reference was built by version {reference_changed} of "
                      f"the rules, this one by version {record['reference_version']}."]
    if notes:
        lines += ['', '### Worse than last week', ''] + [f'- {n}' for n in notes]
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument('--bin', required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--corpora', default=corpora.DEFAULT_DIR)
    parser.add_argument('--corpus', action='append', default=[])
    parser.add_argument('--work', default=os.path.join(ROOT, '.corpora', 'work'))
    parser.add_argument('--runs', type=int, default=5)
    parser.add_argument('--oracle', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('--previous')
    parser.add_argument('--out')
    parser.add_argument('--markdown')
    parser.add_argument('--issue')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    work = os.path.abspath(args.work)
    os.makedirs(work, exist_ok=True)
    version = subprocess.run([args.bin, '--version'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    record = {'caliper': version, 'runs': args.runs, 'reference_version': REFERENCE_VERSION,
              'corpora': {c['name']: measure(args, c, work) for c in selected(args.corpus)}}
    notes = []
    reference_changed = None
    if args.previous and os.path.exists(args.previous):
        with open(args.previous) as f:
            previous = json.load(f)
        notes = findings(record, previous)
        if not same_reference(record, previous):
            reference_changed = previous.get('reference_version', 1)
    table = markdown(record, notes, reference_changed)
    print(table)
    for path, content in ((args.out, json.dumps(record, indent=2) + '\n'), (args.markdown, table),
                          (args.issue, 'The weekly record got worse:\n\n' + '\n'.join(f'- {n}' for n in notes) + '\n'
                           if notes else None)):
        if path and content:
            with open(path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(content)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

name: Weekly

# Caliper, react-docgen-typescript and react-docgen on five public repos with their dependencies installed: time,
# memory and recall (docs/measurement.md). It compares with last week's record and opens or updates one issue when
# Caliper got slower, bigger or less complete. It never runs on a pull request and never fails one.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"

jobs:
  weekly:
    name: Weekly
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      # The corpora's own package managers run under Node 24: Yarn 4.18, which Mantine and React Spectrum pin, crashes
      # under the repository's Node 26 ("Dynamic require of "util" is not supported"). This step comes before the
      # toolchain's so that the toolchain's Node stays first on PATH for everything else; only the installs use this one.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          package-manager-cache: false
      - id: corpus-node
        run: echo "dir=$(dirname "$(command -v node)")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # RDT, react-docgen and the oracle run from apps/oracle's dependencies.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
      # About 10 GB of installed node_modules is too large to cache; the package managers' stores are not.
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .corpora/caches
          key: weekly-${{ hashFiles('scripts/corpora.py', 'pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
      # A corpus that fails to install is named in the log with the tail of the install log; the others still install.
      - name: Fetch and install the corpora
        env:
          INSTALL_NODE_DIR: ${{ steps.corpus-node.outputs.dir }}
        run: python3 scripts/corpora.py setup --install-node-dir "$INSTALL_NODE_DIR"
      - name: Fetch last week's record
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          id=$(gh run list --workflow weekly.yml --status success --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId // empty')
          if [ -n "$id" ]; then gh run download "$id" --name weekly --dir previous; fi
      - name: Measure
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/weekly.py --bin target/release/caliper-docgen --oracle --previous previous/weekly.json
          --out weekly.json --markdown weekly.md --issue issue.md
      - if: always()
        run: cat weekly.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: weekly
          path: |
            weekly.json
            weekly.md
            .corpora/logs
          if-no-files-found: ignore
      - name: Open or update the issue
        if: ${{ hashFiles('issue.md') != '' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh label create weekly-measurement --description "Caliper got worse in the weekly record" --color D93F0B 2>/dev/null || true
          existing=$(gh issue list --label weekly-measurement --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body-file issue.md
          else
            gh issue create --title "The weekly record got worse" --label weekly-measurement --body-file issue.md
          fi

1	// TypeScript 7.1's checker as a test oracle for Caliper's prop types (docs/parity.md). Test-only: the opt-in semantic
2	// backend is a separate, experimental feature.
3	//
4	// For one corpus, finds components the way react-docgen-typescript does (an exported function whose only or `props`
5	// parameter is the props type), reads each prop's type from the checker, and compares it structurally with the prop
6	// Caliper's canonical JSON reports for the same component (src/oracle-compare.ts). Each shared prop gets one verdict:
7	//
8	//   identical          both sides describe the same type
9	//   spelled            the same type, Caliper by name where the checker expands it, or the reverse
10	//   less precise       Caliper's type is looser or unevaluated (an opaque type, `string` for a literal union, a name
11	//                      left unexpanded, a lost optional or rest parameter, a missing field)
12	//   wrong              Caliper's type describes something else
13	//   checker any/error  the checker itself has no type (an unresolved import, `any`, or `unknown` where Caliper has one)
14	//
15	// Checker types are normalized once per type id and verdicts made once per (Caliper prop, checker type), so Chakra's
16	// ~470,000 props cost a few thousand distinct comparisons.
17	//
18	import { readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
19	import { join, relative } from 'node:path'
20	import { API, SignatureKind, SymbolFlags } from 'typescript-beta/sync'
21	import { checkerNormalizer } from './oracle-checker.ts'
22	import { caliperNorm, compare, VERDICTS, type Norm, type Verdict } from './oracle-compare.ts'
23	
24	const KEYS = ['root', 'src', 'tsconfig', 'caliper', 'out', 'files', 'dump', 'rows', 'missing'] as const
25	const args: Partial<Record<(typeof KEYS)[number], string>> = {}
26	for (let i = 2; i < process.argv.length; i += 2) {
27	  args[process.argv[i].replace(/^--/, '') as (typeof KEYS)[number]] = process.argv[i + 1]
28	}
29	if (!args.root || !args.src || !args.tsconfig || !args.caliper || !args.out) {
30	  console.error('usage: tsx src/oracle.ts --root DIR --src DIR --tsconfig FILE --caliper FILE --out FILE')
31	  process.exit(2)
32	}
33	const root = realpathSync(args.root)
34	
35	function walk(dir: string): string[] {
36	  const out: string[] = []
37	  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
38	    if (entry.name === 'node_modules') continue
39	    const path = join(dir, entry.name)
40	    if (entry.isDirectory()) out.push(...walk(path))
41	    else out.push(path)
42	  }
43	  return out
44	}
45	
46	const files: string[] = args.files
47	  ? readFileSync(args.files, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean)
48	  : walk(realpathSync(args.src))
49	      .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.tsx'))
50	      .toSorted()
51	
52	const api = new API({ cwd: root })
53	const programStart = performance.now()
54	// The same program react-docgen-typescript parses in scripts/weekly.py: the component files, with the tsconfig it
55	// uses. The options go through `parseConfigFile` because the 7.1 beta's server panics on string-valued enum options
56	// passed to `createProgram` directly.
57	const { options } = api.parseConfigFile(args.tsconfig)
58	const program = api.createProgram(files, options)
59	const { checker } = program.getProject()
60	const programMs = performance.now() - programStart
61	const checkerNorm = checkerNormalizer(checker)
62	
63	// ─── Components ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
64	
65	const normComponent = (name: string) =>
66	  (
67	    name
68	      .replace(/ \(.*\)$/, '')
69	      .split('/')
70	      .at(-1) ?? ''
71	  )
72	    .split('.')
73	    .at(-1)!
74	    .replaceAll(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '')
75	const rel = (path: string) => relative(root, realpathSync(path))
76	const pathKey = (path: string) =>
77	  process.platform === 'darwin' || process.platform === 'win32' ? path.toLowerCase() : path
78	
79	const caliper = JSON.parse(readFileSync(args.caliper, 'utf8'))
80	const caliperByFile = new Map<string, { name: string; key: string; component: any }[]>()
81	for (const [componentKey, component] of Object.entries<any>(caliper.components)) {
82	  // Schema 2 lists a component's prop set ids, each a map of prop name to prop id; this reads one map of both.
83	  if (Array.isArray(component.props)) {
84	    component.props = Object.assign({}, ...component.props.map((id: string) => caliper.propSets[id]))
85	  }
86	  const key = rel(component.filePath)
87	  const list = caliperByFile.get(key) ?? []
88	  list.push({ name: normComponent(component.displayName), key: componentKey, component })
89	  caliperByFile.set(key, list)
90	}
91	
92	/** The props type of a component export, the way react-docgen-typescript finds it. */
93	function propsTypeOf(exported: any): any | undefined {
94	  const symbol = exported.flags & SymbolFlags.Alias ? checker.getAliasedSymbol(exported) : exported
95	  const type = checker.getTypeOfSymbol(symbol)
96	  for (const sig of checker.getSignaturesOfType(type, SignatureKind.Call)) {
97	    const params = sig.getParameters()
98	    if (params.length === 1 || params[0]?.name === 'props') return checker.getTypeOfSymbol(params[0])
99	  }
100	  for (const sig of checker.getSignaturesOfType(type, SignatureKind.Construct)) {
101	    if (sig.getParameters().length > 1) continue
102	    const props = checker.getPropertyOfType(sig.getReturnType(), 'props')
103	    if (props) return checker.getTypeOfSymbol(props)
104	  }
105	  return undefined
106	}
107	
108	/** A default export is named by what it exports: the aliased declaration, or the function or class itself. */
109	function exportName(exported: any): string {
110	  if (exported.name !== 'default') return exported.name
111	  if (exported.flags & SymbolFlags.Alias) return checker.getAliasedSymbol(exported).name
112	  return checker.getTypeOfSymbol(exported).getSymbol()?.name ?? 'default'
113	}
114	
115	interface Example {
116	  component: string
117	  prop: string
118	  caliper: unknown
119	  checker: string
120	  normalized: object
121	}
122	const counts = Object.fromEntries(VERDICTS.map((v) => [v, 0])) as Record<Verdict, number>
123	const examples = Object.fromEntries(VERDICTS.map((v) => [v, [] as Example[]])) as Record<Verdict, Example[]>
124	const verdictCache = new Map<string, Verdict>()
125	const rows: [string, string, Verdict | 'missing' | 'collapsed'][] = []
126	const missingDetails: { key: string; prop: string; verdict: 'missing' | 'collapsed'; declarations: string[] }[] = []
127	const dumped: {
128	  key: string
129	  file: string
130	  component: string
131	  prop: string
132	  verdict: Verdict
133	  caliper: unknown
134	  checker: string
135	}[] = []
136	const totals = {
137	  componentsChecker: 0,
138	  componentsMatched: 0,
139	  propsChecker: 0,
140	  propsShared: 0,
141	  propsMissing: 0,
142	  propsCollapsed: 0,
143	  failedExports: 0,
144	  ambiguousExports: 0,
145	}
146	
147	/** The verdict for one prop, made once per (Caliper prop, checker type). */
148	function judge({
149	  component,
150	  prop,
151	  caliperId,
152	  type,
153	}: {
154	  component: string
155	  prop: string
156	  caliperId: string
157	  type: any
158	}) {
159	  const key = `${caliperId}:${type.id}`
160	  const cached = verdictCache.get(key)
161	  if (cached !== undefined) return cached
162	  const c: Norm = caliperNorm(caliper.props[caliperId].type)
163	  const k: Norm = checkerNorm(type)
164	  const verdict = compare(c, k)
165	  verdictCache.set(key, verdict)
166	  if (examples[verdict].length < 20) {
167	    const checkerText = checker.typeToString(type)
168	    examples[verdict].push({
169	      component,
170	      prop,
171	      caliper: caliper.props[caliperId].type,
172	      checker: checkerText,
173	      normalized: { caliper: c, checker: k },
174	    })
175	  }
176	  return verdict
177	}
178	
179	/** Every prop of one exported component the checker finds, against Caliper's component of the same name. */
180	function visitExport(exported: any, candidates: { name: string; key: string; component: any }[], file: string): void {
181	  let propsType
182	  try {
183	    propsType = propsTypeOf(exported)
184	  } catch {
185	    totals.failedExports++
186	    return
187	  }
188	  if (!propsType) return
189	  const props = checker.getPropertiesOfType(propsType)
190	  if (props.length === 0) return
191	  totals.componentsChecker++
192	  const name = exportName(exported)
193	  // React's DOM attributes are one inherited layer; ref and key are deliberately absent from Caliper's output.
194	  const own = props.filter(
195	    (p: any) =>
196	      p.name !== 'ref' &&
197	      p.name !== 'key' &&
198	      !p.declarations?.some((d: any) => String(d.path).includes('/@types/react/')),
199	  )
200	  totals.propsChecker += own.length
201	  const matches = candidates.filter((c) => c.name === normComponent(name))
202	  if (matches.length > 1) {
203	    totals.ambiguousExports++
204	    return
205	  }
206	  const [match] = matches
207	  if (!match) return
208	  totals.componentsMatched++
209	  const shared = own.filter((p: any) => p.name in match.component.props)
210	  const layerFiles = new Set(
211	    (match.component.inheritance ?? [])
212	      .filter((layer: any) => layer.totalProps > 30)
213	      .map((layer: any) => pathKey(String(layer.fileName))),
214	  )
215	  const absent = own.filter((p: any) => !(p.name in match.component.props))
216	  const collapsed: any[] = []
217	  const missing: any[] = []
218	  for (const p of absent) {
219	    if (p.declarations?.some((d: any) => layerFiles.has(pathKey(String(d.path))))) collapsed.push(p)
220	    else missing.push(p)
221	  }
222	  totals.propsMissing += missing.length
223	  totals.propsCollapsed += collapsed.length
224	  if (args.rows) rows.push(...missing.map((p: any) => [match.key, p.name, 'missing'] as [string, string, 'missing']))
225	  if (args.rows)
226	    rows.push(...collapsed.map((p: any) => [match.key, p.name, 'collapsed'] as [string, string, 'collapsed']))
227	  if (args.missing) {
228	    for (const [verdict, absentProps] of [
229	      ['missing', missing],
230	      ['collapsed', collapsed],
231	    ] as const) {
232	      for (const p of absentProps) {
233	        missingDetails.push({
234	          key: match.key,
235	          prop: p.name,
236	          verdict,
237	          declarations: p.declarations?.map((d: any) => String(d.path)) ?? [],
238	        })
239	      }
240	    }
241	  }
242	  if (shared.length === 0) return
243	  const types = checker.getTypeOfSymbol(shared)
244	  for (const [i, p] of shared.entries()) {
245	    totals.propsShared++
246	    const caliperId = match.component.props[p.name]
247	    const verdict = judge({ component: name, prop: p.name, caliperId, type: types[i] })
248	    counts[verdict]++
249	    if (args.rows) rows.push([match.key, p.name, verdict])
250	    if (args.dump && (verdict === 'wrong' || verdict === 'less precise')) {
251	      dumped.push({
252	        key: match.key,
253	        file: rel(file),
254	        component: name,
255	        prop: p.name,
256	        verdict,
257	        caliper: caliper.props[caliperId].type,
258	        checker: checker.typeToString(types[i]),
259	      })
260	    }
261	  }
262	}
263	
264	const start = performance.now()
265	for (const file of files) {
266	  const moduleSymbol = checker.getSymbolOfSourceFile(file)
267	  if (!moduleSymbol) continue
268	  const candidates = caliperByFile.get(rel(file)) ?? []
269	  for (const exported of checker.getExportsOfModule(moduleSymbol)) visitExport(exported, candidates, file)
270	}
271	const compareMs = performance.now() - start
272	
273	const report = {
274	  components_checker: totals.componentsChecker,
275	  components_matched: totals.componentsMatched,
276	  props_checker: totals.propsChecker,
277	  props_shared: totals.propsShared,
278	  props_missing: totals.propsMissing,
279	  props_collapsed: totals.propsCollapsed,
280	  verdicts: counts,
281	  distinct_comparisons: verdictCache.size,
282	  failed_exports: totals.failedExports,
283	  ambiguous_exports: totals.ambiguousExports,
284	  program_ms: Math.round(programMs),
285	  compare_ms: Math.round(compareMs),
286	  examples,
287	}
288	writeFileSync(args.out, JSON.stringify(report, null, 2))
289	if (args.dump) writeFileSync(args.dump, JSON.stringify(dumped))
290	if (args.rows) writeFileSync(args.rows, JSON.stringify(rows))
291	if (args.missing) writeFileSync(args.missing, JSON.stringify(missingDetails))
292	program.dispose()
293	api.close()
294	console.error(
295	  `${totals.componentsMatched}/${totals.componentsChecker} components, ${totals.propsShared} shared props, ` +
296	    `${verdictCache.size} distinct comparisons, program ${(programMs / 1000).toFixed(1)} s, ` +
297	    `compare ${(compareMs / 1000).toFixed(1)} s`,
298	)

12	workflow to open or update one issue with. Nothing here fails a pull request.
13	
14	Usage: scripts/weekly.py --bin BIN [--corpus NAME]... [--corpora DIR] [--work DIR] [--runs N] [--oracle]
15	                         [--previous FILE] [--out FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--issue FILE]
16	"""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The weekly record: Caliper, react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on the five pinned corpora.

For each corpus it records, per tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start included), and for
Caliper the canonical JSON's size. Recall is measured against RDT: of the components RDT reports with props, how many
the tool also reports (same file, same name), and of their props, how many it lists, split into the props `@types/react`
declares and the rest. react-docgen reads each file alone, so it lists none of React's. With --oracle it also records
how often TypeScript 7.1's checker contradicts Caliper's prop types. That is information, never a gate.

--previous FILE compares with an earlier record (the last green run's artifact) and, when Caliper is more than 10%
slower or uses more than 10% more memory, or its recall falls by more than 2 points, writes --issue FILE for the
workflow to open or update one issue with. Nothing here fails a pull request.

Usage: scripts/weekly.py --bin BIN [--corpus NAME]... [--corpora DIR] [--work DIR] [--runs N] [--oracle]
                         [--previous FILE] [--out FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--issue FILE]
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

import corpora
from corpora import ROOT, run_once, selected

SLOWER = 1.10
RECALL_DROP = 0.02
# The rules that decide what the reference is: the exclusions and the pairing. Raise it when a change to them moves recall,
# so that a record is never compared on recall with one made under other rules (a record without it is version 1).
REFERENCE_VERSION = 2


def norm_name(name):
    """A component name as the tools may spell it: no `(file)` suffix, namespace or punctuation."""
    name = re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', name).split('/')[-1].split('.')[-1]
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', name.lower())


def relative(path, root):
    """`path` relative to `root`, both through symlinks: Caliper reports canonical paths, RDT the ones it was given."""
    return os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(path), os.path.realpath(root))


def program_inputs(name, src, out_dir):
    """The component files (every `.tsx` under the source directory) and a tsconfig rooted there."""
    files = []
    for current, dirs, names in os.walk(src):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d != 'node_modules']
        files += [os.path.join(current, n) for n in names if n.endswith('.tsx')]
    list_file = os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.files.txt')
    with open(list_file, 'w') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(sorted(files)) + '\n')
    tsconfig = os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.tsconfig.json')
    with open(tsconfig, 'w') as f:
        json.dump({
            'include': [f'{src}/**/*.ts', f'{src}/**/*.tsx'],
            'compilerOptions': {'target': 'ES2022', 'module': 'ESNext', 'moduleResolution': 'bundler', 'jsx': 'react-jsx',
                                'strict': True, 'skipLibCheck': True, 'noEmit': True},
        }, f, indent=2)
    return list_file, tsconfig


def tool_run(command, out):
    """One whole run of a Node tool that writes its components to `out`: wall ms, peak RSS MiB and the components."""
    seconds, rss = run_once(command)
    with open(out) as f:
        return {'ms': round(seconds * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(rss)}, json.load(f)['components']


def caliper_run(binary, src, runs):
    """Median wall ms and peak RSS MiB of `extract --json` with dependency loading on, and the JSON's size."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--load-dependencies']
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
        run_once(command, stdout=out)
        size = out.tell()
    samples = [run_once(command) for _ in range(runs)]
    return {'ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in samples) * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(max(r for _, r in samples)),
            'json_mb': round(size / 2**20, 2)}


def caliper_components(binary, src, root):
    """Caliper's components in RDT's format, as (file, name) -> prop names."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--format', 'rdt', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported',
               '--quiet', '--load-dependencies']
    out = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return {(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName'])): set(c['props'])
            for c in json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]).values()}


def caliper_layer_members(binary, src, root):
    """The props Caliper's collapsed inheritance layers hold, as (file, name) -> prop names: the output names them in a
    layer instead of listing them as props (ADR 0012), and the canonical JSON is the one that carries the layers."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported', '--quiet',
               '--load-dependencies']
    out = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    document = json.loads(out[out.index('{'):])
    lists = document.get('nameLists', {})
    members = {}
    for c in document['components'].values():
        names = set()
        for layer in c.get('inheritance', []):
            if layer.get('members'):
                names |= set(lists[layer['members']])
        members[(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName']))] = names
    return members


LIB_FILE = re.compile(r'/typescript/lib/lib\.[^/]*\.d\.ts$')
REACT_DIR = 'node_modules/@types/react/'
EXTENSIONS = ('', '.tsx', '.ts', '/index.tsx', '/index.ts')
# An identifier inside any number of calls (`memo(forwardRef(Foo))`, `React.memo(Foo)`, `Object.assign(Foo, {...})`),
# followed by what ends an argument or an expression: `, ) ; !`, a type assertion or the end of the line.
WRAPPED = r'(?:[\w.]+\s*(?:<[^>]*>)?\s*\(\s*)*(\w+)(?=\s*[,);!]|\s+as\b|\s+satisfies\b|\s*$)'


def declared_in_react(info):
    return REACT_DIR in (info.get('parent') or '')
